facts.text: Wilmington Manor sits at 39°41′12″N 75°35′04″W, placing it just northwest of New Castle and south of Wilmington.
The area that became Wilmington Manor grew under Dutch control in the mid‑1600s, with New Castle’s Fort Casimir founded in 1651 becoming Delaware’s first capital from 1704 to 1777.
Wilmington Manor’s landscape reflects a sedimentary history, with Cretaceous marine and fluvial deposits reshaped by post‑glacial sea‑level changes.
Wilmington University’s main campus is located within the Wilmington Manor census‑designated place, making it a hub for higher education in the area.
Wilmington Manor’s landscape features minimal topographic variation, which has made urban development straightforward.
The area encompassing modern Wilmington Manor traces its roots to early colonial settlements along the Delaware River, influenced by 17th‑century Dutch and Swedish explorers.
